questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Level of the local university, culture of the destination, availability of courses I am interested in and experiences of my friends who have went on exchnages before.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I would rate my exchange experience positively, however there were minor issues, especially with the administration of the hosting university. The courses that I thought I would participate in were not available, even though they were promised to be available. Apart from the described issues, the experience was great, everyone was friendly, I met a lot of great people - students and teachers. I also got to experience how different academic institutions work.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy, however I was in a privilged situation as I speak the native language of the destination country. For students who do not speak Polish, I believe it can be a lot more challenging, as a lot of university's announcements and communication was in Polish. However, I try to support my friends and translate stuff they were struggling with. Apart form the language barrier in the communication sometimes, the information was fairly available online and it was possible to contact the administraion at any time.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have received quite a lot of assistance, especially with the administration issues. There were some issues with signing up for courses and ECTS points received for them however after exchange of numerous emails the issues were resolved and some uncertainties were explained. Overall, the assistance I achieved was ok and the staff really wanted to help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I am satisfied with the assistance available to students however I feel like there should be more assistance in the context of legalizing the stay (legal permits etc.)

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The housing was easy for me to find as I am a Polish national. For students coming on exchange to Warsaw, who do not want to live in a dormitory, I would recommend to look for housing through Facebook however people should beware of potential scams. Most local people find housing through facebook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Even though it is way more expensive than living in a dorm, I really recommend it as it enables you to experience life like a local. Private apartments also have a way better standard than university's dorms which are really outdated and uncomfortable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The availability of dorms was high however due to their standard I decided to go for phousing off campus. They are a good option though for people who want to get affordable housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The process was very easy, I did not have any difficulties with it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process was announced through an email. On the university's website where the registration took place, there were clear instructions how to proceed. There were no issues with the registration process, it was fairly easy and well described so did not cause any major difficulties.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could contact the staff through e-mail which was the most popular way of contact. It was also possible to contact the staff by phone or to talk to them in person in the office on campus. All the staff was welcoming and helpful most of the times.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As the classes that were intitially announced to be available at the end were not, I had to find different classes. Personally, that was not a big issue as the other classes that I signed up for were quite similar to the classes I initially wanted to register for. The variety of classes students could sign up for was really comprehensive.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The process is not overly complicated however if you have any questions or doubts, do not hesitate to ask the staff for help, they are there to help you. You can also ask the local students for help if you feel more comfortable with that.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In general I was satisfied with the academic programme however not all classes that were promised to be held were available for registration during the winter semester. Some classes were instead available in the summer semester which did not work for most for the students as in the summer semester different classes had to be taken up.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses really varied. Some courses were very advanced and were suitable for Master students, while other ones were definitely introductive courses with basic knowledge and explanations of basic concepts. It would be great if it was described more thorougly in the online catalogue of courses what is the level of each course so that no one is disappointed or struggling in class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
he academic style in general was noticeably different between the two universities. Classes at UCPH were typically structured around active discussion, encouraging students to participate, share their perspectives, and critically engage with the material during each session. In contrast, at UW the teaching format tended to be more traditional and centered on lectures, where the professor delivered the content and students listened and took notes, with fewer opportunities for spontaneous group debate.
Another significant difference concerned preparation for classes. At UCPH, it was expected that students would read several academic articles or chapters before most sessions, meaning that the discussion in class could build on previous independent study. This approach required students to stay consistently up to date with the reading material. At UW, however, such preparation was not required for the majority of courses, and readings—if assigned—were often supplementary rather than essential for participation in class.
Despite these differences in teaching style and expectations, the grading systems at both institutions were relatively similar. In both cases, assessment commonly took the form of written essays, oral examinations, presentations, or project reports. As a result, although the learning environment and classroom dynamic varied, the methods used to evaluate students’ knowledge and understanding were largely comparable across the two universities.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend the course “Geopolitical Tuesdays,” which I took during the first semester of my exchange program. It turned out to be one of the most engaging and intellectually stimulating courses I attended. Throughout the classes, a wide range of current and relevant global topics were explored in depth, allowing students to gain a better understanding of the rapidly changing geopolitical landscape.
What made the course particularly interesting was the diversity of guest lecturers. Many sessions were conducted by researchers and experts from different academic backgrounds, frequently representing foreign universities. This provided a unique opportunity to hear multiple perspectives, often shaped by the political and social environments of the lecturers’ home countries.
The primary focus of the course was on analyzing contemporary international issues, including global power dynamics, regional conflicts, and emerging political trends. Thanks to its practical approach and exposure to experts from abroad, “Geopolitical Tuesdays” offered a valuable and enriching academic experience that went far beyond standard classroom learning.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There were no unexpected costs that I encountered.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The groceries turned out to be more expensive than I had originally expected. Before arriving, I assumed that everyday food shopping would be significantly cheaper compared to Denmark, but in reality the difference was not as noticeable. Many basic items, such as fresh produce, dairy products, and pantry staples, were priced only slightly lower, and in some cases almost the same as in Danish supermarkets.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The university offered a wide range of non-academic opportunities, making student life vibrant and engaging beyond the classroom. There were numerous social events, such as themed parties, gatherings, and meet-ups that allowed students to connect with others, make new friends, and feel part of the university community.
In addition to this, the institution organized various sports events, giving students the chance to stay active, try different physical activities, and participate in both recreational and competitive formats. These activities helped create a well-rounded campus environment where wellbeing and social interaction were encouraged.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were lots of activities available, mainly related to sports, languages and different cultures.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would like to recommend participation in the events during orientation as they allow you the make a lot of friends from different courses and participate in fun activities such as pub crawls and sightiseeing of the city center.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to go to Krakow and Gdansk, visit museums in Warsaw such as the Jewish history museum.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I was easy as I am Polish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to learn some basic phrases in Polish, as it can make a noticeable difference in everyday interactions and help local people become more open to socializing. Even simple expressions like greeting someone, thanking them, or ordering something politely can show appreciation for the local culture and effort on your part.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences between Poland and Denmark. In Poland people seem a bit more open to helping and talking to strangers.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciate the local cuisine the most.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to learn a few basic phrases in Polish, try the local cuisine, take some extra language classes and participate in the free sports classes available at the university - they are really good and the sports facilities are great.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to take advantage of the language and sports courses offered at the host institution, as these opportunities are often unique and not easily available elsewhere. At many universities, such courses either do not exist or require additional fees, whereas during an exchange they are frequently included as part of the student experience.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of the experience was successfully defending my Master’s thesis, which I had spent the entire summer semester writing. After months of research, planning, drafting, revising, and refining my arguments, standing in front of the committee and presenting my findings felt like a true culmination of the effort I had put in.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The greatest challenge I faced was finding a supervisor for my thesis, primarily because I had no prior experience or established connections with lecturers at the host institution. Unlike at my home university, where I already knew the teaching staff and had a sense of their research interests, academic styles, and personalities, at the new university I had to make this decision without any previous interaction or insight.

This made the selection process more difficult, as choosing a supervisor is not only about matching research topics but also about finding someone with whom you can communicate effectively and feel supported during the writing process. Since I lacked personal familiarity with the faculty, I had to rely on course descriptions, staff profiles, and recommendations from other students to make an informed choice. Overall, it was a challenging situation that required careful consideration and a degree of trust in making such an important academic decision without the benefit of existing relationships.
